chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

We performed Hajj and we were first-timers, so we performed Sa'ee between As-Safa and Al-Marwa for fourteen circuits. So I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; seven are for you and seven are dropped.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the two hills between which Sa'ee is performed)
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa (one of the two hills between which Sa'ee is performed)
key_terms.شَوْطاً: Circuits (plural of shat, referring to the back-and-forth movements between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.صَرُورَةٌ: First-timer (one performing Hajj or Umrah for the first time)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I perform 14 circuits of Sa'ee during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who performs fourteen circuits of Sa'ee, validating the act by counting seven as obligatory and the remaining seven as surplus. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding ritual completeness, distinguishing between the minimum requirement for validity and the recommended practice. It serves as a practical guide for pilgrims who may inadvertently exceed the standard number of circuits, ensuring their Hajj or Umrah remains spiritually and legally sound.
